messages:
sasha: Heads-up, na-east3 control plane health alert. Auth proxies returning 5xx and we’re seeing GPU pod evictions in the prod-gpu pool. Console is partially unresponsive (UI stuck on loading).
kyra-oncall: Confirmed. Seen a spike of controlplane leader failovers + authz latency. K8s events show a flurry of 'Evicted: node.kubernetes.io/memory-pressure' on GPU nodes.
raj: Copy. Any indication this is a kubelet-level OOM or something higher in the control plane?
maya: Logs from provisioner show rate-limit backoffs to the cluster manager and provisioning RPC timeouts to na-east3-controlplane. Suspect controlplane API flaps -> controllers failing to reconcile, leading to pod pressure.
infra-bot: incident created: INC-2026-2173456789 (severity P1) — assigned to kyra-oncall. Auto-annotated resources: prod-gpu, na-east3-controlplane, auth-proxy.
kyra-oncall: Quick mitigation plan: 1) shift new user traffic off na-east3 via global router to na-central1/na-west2 for 15m 2) enable dedicated burst capacity for redwood-dedicated-gpu prod pool (if capacity available) 3) run controlplane leader restart on na-east3 nodes if still flapping.
sasha: Agree. Raj/Maya—can you run the traffic-shift? We need to avoid cascading evictions.
raj: On it. Pushing route update to edge-router: set weight na-east3=0.2 -> na-central1=0.5, na-west2=0.3. Command: 
```
edgectl traffic update --service inference-api --region na-east3 --weights na-central1=0.5,na-west2=0.3,na-east3=0.2
```
raj: Applied, watching 2xx/5xx.
maya: Observing drop in new connections to na-east3 within ~30s. 5xx rate from auth-proxy down 40%, but existing long-lived requests to na-east3 still failing and causing client retries.
oliver: Can we scale up the provisioner in na-east3? Job queue backlog is causing retries. If we can bump worker count it might clear pods quicker. Cost heads-up: extra workers will blow weekly GPU overtime if sustained.
kyra-oncall: Tried horizontal scaling via autoscaler but controlplane API failed to accept the scale request. Manual scaling attempted?
raj: Manual scale requires patching provisioner via kube API; controlplane auth failing prevents that. We're in a chicken-and-egg.
sketchy-mitigation: Could we temporarily use cross-region provisioning (spawn GPUs in na-central on behalf of na-east3 tenants)? That offloads some creation ops to healthy controlplane region.
maya: Cross-region provisioning path exists but needs a config toggle in mgmtplane. I can flip it but will need a short maintenance window and coordinate data-plane routing for KV secrets (KMS).
sasha: Do it. Prioritize customer traffic. Make the change and announce maintenance.
maya: Flipped cross-region-provisioning flag to true. Verified worker tasks accepted in na-central1. New pods provisioning successfully in na-central and binding to inference endpoints.
raj: Noticed an uptick in token-based auth failures for some sessions - likely stale auth caches referencing na-east3 token endpoints. Can we warm caches or failover auth token endpoints to na-central?
kyra-oncall: Implementing fallback for auth token fetch to na-central1. This is a config push to auth-proxy: set token_endpoints:[na-central1, na-east3]. Pushing now.
raj: Auth failures dropped to baseline. Good.
oliver: GPU evictions are tapering but node pressure still high on na-east3 — many pods are terminating and rescheduling to other regions. Storage attach/detach latencies also high.
sasha: Console access remains flaky for some users. Is that purely controlplane API or is the web-proxy in front also suffering?
maya: Web-proxy is fine; it's the console backend calls to controlplane for resource lists that are timing out. We should show a banner on the console about degraded NA-East3 state.
raj: Added banner via frontend config: "Partial outage in na-east3 — some resources may be delayed." Pushed.
intra-decision: Are we going to failover leader in na-east3 controlplane nodes (force restart) or wait for gradual recovery?
kyra-oncall: Recommendation: force a controlled restart of controlplane leader nodes in staggered fashion (to avoid quorum loss). I’ll coordinate with infra SRE.
oliver: Be careful — if quorum lost, multi-region failover could be messy. Stagger 30s between restarts and monitor leader election.
kyra-oncall: Restart sequence initiated: ctrl-maestro-01 -> ctrl-maestro-02 (30s delay) -> ctrl-maestro-03.
infra-bot: controlplane restart events logged (ctrl-maestro-01 restarted by kyra-oncall).
kyra-oncall: After restarts, API latency improved from 800ms -> 120ms p95. Controlplane reconciler queue drained ~60% in the first 3m.
maya: Provisioner regained ability to accept scale requests. Manually scaled provisioner replica count from 3 -> 6 to clear backlog (short-term).
oliver: Good. Cost estimate: that temp scale adds ~18 GPU-hours/day on average for the week if sustained. Notify finance and product if we need longer.
sasha: Thanks team. Next steps: 1) leave cross-region provisioning enabled for 2 hours, 2) monitor for any data consistency issues, 3) prepare rollback flag, 4) finance will be notified if extra capacity persists beyond 24h. Anyone object?
raj: No objections. Will monitor traffic and auth metrics.
maya: Will watch for storage attach errors and KV replication lag.
oliver: I’ll prepare a short post-incident blurb for customers if we fully recover.
kyra-oncall: Marking incident as mitigated for customer traffic at 2173460000; keeping P1 until all queues drained and console fully responsive.
deploy-bot: rollout notice: no user-facing deploys allowed for inference-api while P1 active.
sasha: OK locking PRs for inference-api and provisioner until we close. Good work.
kyra-oncall: Will post a fuller timeline and RCA draft in #postmortems once we’ve stabilized.
